subject.title: feat(onboard): recommendations store with once-semantics and self-naming bootstrap

question: Should OpenClaw make onboarding recommendations a durable shared-state, once-only offer that is handed from the wizard to the first-run bootstrap through two new `onboard recommendations` CLI commands?
rationale: This is a new persistent product behavior and public CLI contract, not a narrow correction to an already-defined broken behavior; the `maintainer` label requires human confirmation of the permanent onboarding direction.

options.title: Approve the durable onboarding contract
options.body: Keep the persistent store and CLI handoff after reviewing upgrade behavior and receiving real after-fix proof for the final head.

options.title: Keep recommendations in the wizard only
options.body: Avoid the new cross-process state and bootstrap command contract, accepting that the proposed deferred ceremony design will need a different owner-approved mechanism.

options.title: Split state/CLI from bootstrap copy
options.body: Land or review the product contract separately from the bootstrap-template rewrite so each user-visible decision has narrower validation.

recommendation.title: Approve the durable onboarding contract
recommendation.body: Keep the persistent store and CLI handoff after reviewing upgrade behavior and receiving real after-fix proof for the final head.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR context identifies steipete as the author of the cited onboarding redesign and the implementation, making them the closest available routing candidate for the design decision.
